pr.title: Have the CLI find a moved store in the app's iCloud container
pr.head: ccefa4563bc2f45b8a5407f402c5d09458e17244

summary: multipass is a command-line password manager whose store is a package: a folder of encrypted files, by default ~/.multipass/store.multipass. The passkeys plan adds a Mac and iPhone app that keeps that package in the app's iCloud container, the app's own folder in iCloud Drive, so every device shares one store. On a Mac, the app moves an existing package out of ~/.multipass and into the container.

After that move, ~/.multipass holds no store. At the base, the CLI reached the container only through MULTIPASS_STORE, set from an export line the app shows. Without it, every command found no store, and multipass init would create a second, empty store that no other device sees.

This pull request changes only the plan. It proposes, as § 6 question 10, that when neither --store nor MULTIPASS_STORE is set and ~/.multipass holds neither store.multipass nor store.age, the CLI's default becomes the container's package when it exists. init then finds that package and refuses, and the export line becomes optional. The answer is proposed, not decided, and the question records an alternative: keep ~/.multipass as the default, and have init warn when the container holds a store.

cards.title: Where the CLI looks for the store
cards.html:
1. --store, when passed.
  2. MULTIPASS_STORE, when set.
  3. ~/.multipass/store.multipass, or ~/.multipass/store.age, which the vault-key plan moves into a package.
  4. New: the container's Documents/store.multipass, when it exists.
  5. Otherwise ~/.multipass/store.multipass, where init creates one.

cards.title: Review so far
cards.html:
• One open finding: a store that later appears in ~/.multipass silently takes the CLI off the container.
  • Four suggestions: the container folder's name, a prototype check for a package iCloud has not downloaded, the case where MULTIPASS_STORE still names the old location, and saying question 10 must be answered before the plan is ready.
  • The plan stays draft, so it makes no readiness claim.

groups.title: The CLI's fallback to the container
groups.kicker: Question 10 and the rows of the passkeys plan that follow from it
intro: Every edit is in the passkeys plan. Question 10 in § 6 states the problem and the proposed answer, and the other edits make the rest of the plan agree with that answer.

• § 2.4's table says the CLI finds the container by itself, and that the export line is then optional.
  • § 2.5's src/main.rs row gives the rule and the path, ~/Library/Mobile Documents/<container>/Documents/store.multipass, with the container's identifier as a constant.
  • § 2.5's README.md row says the README documents the fallback.
  • § 4's move row expects multipass list to open the moved package and multipass init to fail with a store already exists at <path>.

checks.text: The container is the app's folder in iCloud Drive. On a Mac it sits under ~/Library/Mobile Documents/. A package there may be listed before its files have downloaded.

files.note: The passkeys plan: question 10 proposes the CLI's fallback to the container, and § 2.4, § 2.5 and § 4 follow it.

checks.text: § 4's expected error matches the one init gives today in run in src/main.rs, a store already exists at <path>, read at the head.

Open finding: the CLI uses the container only while ~/.multipass holds no store, and the export line is now optional. A store that appears there later, such as from init on a second Mac before iCloud Drive lists the package, silently takes over, and its saves reach no other device. The review asks that commands fail naming both paths when both hold a store.
The folder under Mobile Documents is named after the container identifier with each . replaced by ~. The row does not say so yet.
